# L-T-01 — First item

Area: Basics · Kind: foundation · Study first: none
Sources: fixture
Checked against: `main` @ `abc1234`. Written: 2026-01-01.

## 1. Main idea

A small function that adds two numbers.

## 2. The picture

| Input | Output |
| --- | --- |
| a, b | a + b |

## 3. Points to remember

- **It returns the sum** · no side effects · `src/main.c:3`.

## 4. Easy to get wrong

| People often think | In fact |
| --- | --- |
| It checks overflow | It does not (`src/main.c:3`) |

## 5. Prediction questions

1. What does add(2, 3) return?
   <details><summary>Answer</summary>5, `src/main.c:3`.</details>

## 6. Exercises

### Exercise 1 — Understand: find the function

Find the function that adds.

<details><summary>Hint: direction</summary>Look in src.</details>
<details><summary>Hint: specific</summary>It is the only function.</details>
<details><summary>Solution</summary>`add` in `src/main.c:1`.</details>

### Exercise 2 — Apply: change the operator

Predict what happens if + becomes -.

<details><summary>Hint: direction</summary>Think of add(5, 3).</details>
<details><summary>Hint: specific</summary>The result is the difference.</details>
<details><summary>Solution</summary>add(5, 3) returns 2.</details>

### Exercise 3 — Apply advanced: overflow

What happens with the largest int?

<details><summary>Hint: direction</summary>Signed overflow.</details>
<details><summary>Hint: specific</summary>It is undefined behaviour in C.</details>
<details><summary>Solution</summary>Undefined; the code does not guard it.</details>
